info.text:
Average hourly pay rose 3% in the year to September 2026, but prices rose 3.7%, so real hourly pay fell 0.7%. In two days in October, the consumer price index, producer prices (up 6.3% over a year), Freddie Mac's 7.4% mortgage rate and Social Security's 3.6% COLA all told the same story, with the Fed's next decision on Oct 28. This video compares 2026 with the 1970s and with 2021-22, and walks through what it means for paychecks, savings, debt and 401(k)s, with labeled examples.
